stories.headline: Anthropic Launches BioMysteryBench; Claude Mythos Solved ~30% of Questions That Stumped Human Experts

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released BioMysteryBench, a bioinformatics benchmark using 99 real-world challenges with raw, messy datasets from actual research — designed to test creative problem-solving rather than textbook knowledge.
key_facts.excerpt: We developed BioMysteryBench, a bioinformatics benchmark that tasks Claude with the analysis of real-world datasets, while tackling some of the challenges inherent in evaluating complex and noisy biological systems.

key_facts.fact: Claude Mythos solved approximately 30% of 23 questions that a panel of human bioinformatics experts could not answer, sometimes using strategies different from those attempted by humans.
key_facts.excerpt: The latest generations solved many problems that a panel of human experts could not, sometimes using very different strategies.

key_facts.fact: Claude's scientific capabilities in biology are improving rapidly across model generations, with current models performing on par with human experts on the benchmark overall.
key_facts.excerpt: We learned that Claude's scientific capabilities in biology are improving rapidly across generations, that current models perform on par with human experts.

key_facts.fact: Unlike existing benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, GPQA, LAB-Bench), BioMysteryBench focuses on open-ended research problems where there are many valid approaches, mirroring real scientific work.
key_facts.excerpt: These benchmarks move us closer to measuring scientific capability, but they don't quite test whether a model can devise creative solutions to the messy, open-ended problems that define research.

stories.headline: OpenAI Traces GPT-5.1's 'Goblin Problem' to RL Reward Leakage From Nerdy Personality Training

key_facts.fact: Starting with GPT-5.1, OpenAI's models increasingly used goblin and gremlin metaphors; 'goblin' usage rose 175% after GPT-5.1's launch, while 'gremlin' rose 52%.
key_facts.excerpt: When we looked, use of 'goblin' in ChatGPT had risen by 175% after the launch of GPT-5.1, while 'gremlin' had risen by 52%.

key_facts.fact: The root cause was traced to the 'Nerdy' personality customization feature: its RL reward signal consistently scored outputs with creature words higher, even though Nerdy accounted for only 2.5% of responses but 66.7% of all goblin mentions.
key_facts.excerpt: Nerdy accounted for only 2.5% of all ChatGPT responses, but 66.7% of all 'goblin' mentions in ChatGPT responses.

key_facts.fact: The behavior spread via a feedback loop: the RL reward boosted creature-language under the Nerdy prompt, then the style transferred to non-Nerdy contexts through supervised fine-tuning on model-generated rollouts.
key_facts.excerpt: Once a style tic is rewarded, later training can spread or reinforce it elsewhere, especially if those outputs are reused in supervised fine-tuning or preference data.

key_facts.fact: The Nerdy personality reward showed positive uplift for creature-word outputs in 76.2% of datasets audited, confirming systematic bias in the reward signal.
key_facts.excerpt: The Nerdy personality reward showed a clear tendency to score outputs to the same problem with 'goblin' or 'gremlin' higher than outputs without, with positive uplift in 76.2% of datasets.

key_facts.fact: As goblin mentions increased under the Nerdy personality, they increased by nearly the same relative proportion in samples without it, demonstrating cross-context style transfer from RL training.
key_facts.excerpt: As goblin and gremlin mentions increased under the Nerdy personality, they increased by nearly the same relative proportion in samples without it.

sources.title: Where the goblins came from

stories.headline: Samsung Q1 Chip Profit Jumps 49x to Record $36B as Memory Shortage Set to Worsen in 2027

key_facts.fact: Samsung Q1 operating profit reached a record ₩57.2 trillion ($40.1B), with the chip division accounting for ₩53.7 trillion ($36.15B) — a 49-fold year-over-year increase from ₩1.1 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung said January-March operating profit in its cash cow chip division reached a record 53.7 trillion won ($36.15 billion) from just 1.1 trillion won in the same period a year earlier. That made up 94% of the quarter's 57.2 trillion won record total.

key_facts.fact: Revenue rose 69% YoY to ₩133.9 trillion ($93.7B), an all-time quarterly high, beating the analyst estimate of ~₩130 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics said Thursday it posted first-quarter revenue of 133.87 trillion won ($93.7 billion) and operating profit of 57.23 trillion won ($40.1 billion). Revenue rose 69% from a year earlier.

key_facts.fact: Samsung warned the memory supply-demand gap will widen further in 2027: 'Based solely on the demand currently received for 2027, the supply-to-demand gap for 2027 is set to widen even further than in 2026.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Our supply falls far short of customer demand,' said Samsung's Kim Jaejune. 'Based solely on the demand currently received for 2027, the supply-to-demand gap for 2027 is set to widen even further than in 2026.'

key_facts.fact: Samsung started the industry's first mass-production sales of HBM4 chips and SOCAMM2 modules for Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, and will deliver HBM4E samples in Q2 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics added that in the second quarter it will begin shipping customer samples of HBM4E, a next-generation product for next year, rushing to be the first in the industry to supply it following HBM4.

key_facts.fact: HBM revenue is forecast to more than triple this year versus last year, with HBM4's share of total HBM revenue expected to exceed 50% starting in Q3 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Our HBM revenue this year is forecast to surge more than three-fold from last year,' said Park Soon-cheol, Samsung Electronics' CFO. 'Customer demand is concentrated on HBM4 for its differentiated performance, and sales volume is already fully sold out.'

key_facts.fact: Samsung has signed multi-year binding contracts with customers hoping to lock in supplies, and said it expects to increase capital expenditure sharply this year to meet AI demand.
key_facts.excerpt: The world's top memory chipmaker by sales also said it has signed multi-year binding contracts with customers hoping to lock in supplies, without disclosing identities or terms.

key_facts.fact: DRAM ASPs rose roughly 90-95% sequentially from Q4 to Q1, signaling sharp tightening in memory markets tied to AI-driven demand.
key_facts.excerpt: The Memory Business set an all-time high for quarterly revenue and operating profits due to its technological leadership in the memory market and higher average selling price (ASP).

stories.headline: SpaceX Falcon Heavy Returns After 18-Month Gap, Launches ViaSat-3 F3 Satellite

key_facts.fact: SpaceX's Falcon Heavy lifted off at 10:13 a.m. EDT on April 29 from Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A, its first flight since October 2024's Europa Clipper mission.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX's most powerful operational rocket, the Falcon Heavy, lifted off Wednesday carrying a massive communications satellite on its 12th flight since 2018.

key_facts.fact: The mission carried ViaSat-3 F3, a 6.6-ton broadband satellite designed to deliver over 1 Tbps of throughput to the Asia-Pacific region, completing Viasat's three-satellite constellation.
key_facts.excerpt: At roughly 6.6 tons, it is a high-capacity broadband communications satellite designed to deliver more than 1 terabit per second of throughput across the APAC region once on station.

key_facts.fact: Both side boosters successfully landed at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, while the center core was expended.
key_facts.excerpt: the center core was expended, while the two side boosters returned to Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. Both boosters executed successful landings—one at Landing Zone 40 (LZ-40) and the other at Landing Zone 2 (LZ-2).

key_facts.fact: Viasat confirmed initial signal acquisition minutes after satellite separation, confirming the spacecraft is healthy in orbit; service entry is expected by late summer 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The satellite successfully separated from the launch vehicle's upper stage just under five hours after liftoff, with initial signals acquired minutes later, confirming the satellite is healthy in orbit

key_facts.fact: Several additional Falcon Heavy missions are planned for 2026, including the Griffin lunar lander for Artemis and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.
key_facts.excerpt: Today's launch marks the return of Falcon Heavy to the active manifest and points to a busy year ahead. Several additional missions are planned for 2026, including the Griffin lunar lander, which is part of the Artemis program, and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

stories.headline: SpaceX Board Approves Musk Compensation Package Tied to $7.5T Valuation, 1M-Person Mars Colony, and Space Data Centers

key_facts.fact: SpaceX's board approved a compensation plan that grants Elon Musk 200 million super-voting Class B restricted shares if SpaceX reaches a $7.5 trillion market valuation and establishes a permanent human colony on Mars with at least 1 million people.
key_facts.excerpt: the SpaceX board in January approved a pay package for the world's richest man that will award 200 million in super-voting restricted shares if the company hits a market value of US$7.5 trillion and establishes a permanent human colony on Mars with at least 1 million people

key_facts.fact: A second tranche of up to 60.4 million restricted shares vests in tranches as SpaceX's market cap climbs in $500 billion increments up to $6.6 trillion, conditional on operating space-based data centers delivering at least 100 terawatts of compute capacity (equivalent to ~100,000 one-gigawatt nuclear reactors).
key_facts.excerpt: 60 million additional shares—vesting in tranches as the company's market capitalization climbs in $500 billion increments from its current $1.1 trillion to as high as $6.6 trillion ... tied to SpaceX executing an audacious plan to build data centers in space ... 100 terawatts annually

key_facts.fact: Class B shares carry 10 votes each versus 1 vote for Class A; Musk currently holds ~42% of SpaceX equity but controls ~79% of voting power.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk owns roughly 42% of SpaceX's equity but controls about 79% of voting power, a gap created by the super-voting share structure.

key_facts.fact: Musk receives a nominal salary of $54,080 per year from SpaceX (since 2019). The pay packages have no fixed timeline beyond Musk's continued employment.
key_facts.excerpt: He has received a nominal salary from SpaceX of US$54,080 per year since 2019.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX is targeting an IPO around June 28, 2026 (Musk's birthday) at a valuation of approximately $1.75 trillion — meaning the first compensation tranche's $7.5T trigger is more than 4x the IPO valuation.
